question: We can see customers buying trade tools at Bunnings. Design an Officeworks campaign for them.
text:
```campaign
{"name": "New Business Welcome - Bunnings Starters (Always-on)",
 "objective": "Turn members who are setting up a trade business into Officeworks business customers by selling them a laptop, a printer, business cards and signage.",
 "hypothesis": "New starters need office and admin kit they don't have yet, so a timely, need-led offer causes purchases that wouldn't happen otherwise. Established tradies already have this kit and buy anyway.",
 "audience": {"description": "OnePass members flagged as new business starters by their Bunnings trade buying, who don't already buy business supplies at Officeworks and aren't established tradies. Members without data-sharing consent are removed.",
  "spec": {"all":[{"field":"BIZ_STARTER_FLAG","op":"is_true"}],"any":[],"exclude":[{"field":"OW_BUSINESS_BUYER","op":"is_true"},{"field":"PRIOR_TRADE_HISTORY","op":"is_true"}],"channels":["EMAIL","SMS"],"promoted":{"category":"Business Essentials","className":null,"brand":null},"suppress":{"fatigueDays":14,"coldContacts":true,"stockConflict":true},"quadrants":null,"cap":null,"lookalike":null},
  "matched": 1732, "final_audience": 846},
 "channels": ["EMAIL", "SMS"],
 "promoted": {"category": "Business Essentials", "brand": null},
 "offer_id": "off-1",
 "start_date": "2026-11-17", "end_date": "2027-01-31", "budget_aud": 7754,
 "expected": {"incremental_conversions": 30, "lift_pts_low": 3.6, "lift_pts_high": 12.9, "basis": "SizeAudience's STARTER_NEW uplift cell (+3.55 pts on a 5.13% base). The interval is camp-h03's measured lift for STARTER_NEW members (+8.2 pts, 95% CI +3.6 to +12.9)."},
 "guardrails": [{"level": "CAUTION", "message": "An audience built on Bunnings or Kmart purchases needs OnePass data-sharing consent (applied automatically), and copy must speak to the need, never to what was bought at another banner."}],
 "key_evidence": [
  {"label": "camp-h03 lift, STARTER_NEW members", "value": "+8.24 pts"},
  {"label": "camp-h03 overall lift (not significant)", "value": "+2.81 pts"},
  {"label": "SMS lift across all campaigns", "value": "+6.82 pts"},
  {"label": "camp-h04 lift, all Bunnings shoppers", "value": "-1.1 pts"},
  {"label": "Expected net margin", "value": "AUD 6.5K"}],
 "draft": null}
```

I recommend a campaign for **new trade-business starters only**, not everyone buying trade tools. Contacting every Bunnings shopper has already lost money. Of five candidate plays, this one ranks second on expected net margin, behind a back-to-school play for Kmart households.



### The signal
- **How it's built:** a member counts as a new business starter if they bought 3 or more of the 6 Bunnings trade categories within 90 days, with no trade buying in the 4–16 months before. The categories are power tools, specialist tools, ladders, tool storage, workwear/PPE and consumables. That pattern looks like someone setting up a business who needs a laptop, printer, business cards, signage and a business account.
- **Its main weakness:** established tradies buy the same kinds of tools. They already have their setup and mostly buy anyway, so I've excluded them, along with members who already buy business supplies at Officeworks.
- **Size:** 4,358 members bought a trade cluster, but 2,573 of them are established tradies. Only 1,785 are starters.

### Why now
- The signal fades quickly. The playbook says it stays fresh for about four months, after which the member is an established tradie. The opportunity sizing puts the freshest window at about 60 days after the first trade purchase.
- Run it as an **always-on trigger**, not a one-off blast. Today 846 starters made their first trade purchase in the last 60 days, the same number as the final audience.
- The live Black Friday laptop campaign is in the Technology category, so it doesn't clash with this one.

### Who is in and who is left out
- **Funnel:** 1,732 matched. 534 were removed for having no OnePass data-sharing consent. The audience builder applies that rule automatically because the audience uses Bunnings data. 846 remain.
- **Quality:** all 846 are "persuadable" (members who buy more when contacted). The 255 "sleeping dogs" (members who buy less and unsubscribe when contacted) and 279 "lost causes" (members who rarely buy) are left out. No cold contacts remain, and the audience health score is 90.
- **Mix:** Electrical 180, Carpentry 178, Plumbing 163, Cleaning 162, Landscaping 149.
- **Copy rule:** speak to the need ("setting up your business?"), never to the purchase ("we saw you bought a ladder at Bunnings").

### The offer
- **Main offer:** **New Business Tech Bundle - $150 Off** (off-1): $150 off a laptop over $799 plus a printer, bought in one transaction with a new Officeworks business account.
- **Bundle with:** **Free Business Card Design + 250 Cards** (off-2), **20% Off Signage and Vehicle Magnets** (off-3) and **Officeworks Business Account - Free Sign-Up** (off-4).

### Expected result
- About **30 incremental conversions**, or +3.55 pts on a 5.13% base. Expected net margin is about AUD 6.5K on AUD 7.8K of cost, much of it from follow-on business-account spend.
- **The comparable test:** the New Business Welcome trade cluster test (camp-h03) lifted conversion by **+8.2 pts** (95% CI +3.6 to +12.9) for the starter members this campaign targets. Its overall lift was +2.8 pts and not significant.
- **The broad version failed:** the business account campaign to all Bunnings shoppers (camp-h04) *lowered* conversion by 1.1 pts. Cold contacts did worst, at −1.9 pts.
- **Channels:** SMS is the channel with significant lift (+6.82 pts across all campaigns, +6.1 pts in camp-h03). Email's lift is not significant, but email reaches 745 of the audience against 369 for SMS. Lead with SMS where members have opted in and use email as the follow-up.

### Risks
- The audience is small (846, under 100/month as a trigger), so each month's result will be noisy. Keep a randomised holdout and read results across months together.
- Apple is short in 5 WA stores. Don't feature MacBooks in the WA laptop creative.
- The $150 cost per redemption makes margin depend on follow-on spend. If take-up is weak, lead with the cheaper card and signage offers.
- The signal is a proxy: some people who look like starters will be one-off renovators.

### Other plays
- **School list service for Kmart school-age households** ranks higher overall (expected net margin about AUD 62.6K), but it's a January play.
- **All Bunnings shoppers** (about −AUD 141K expected), **home-office furniture** (about −AUD 1.0K) and **laptop trade-up** (about −AUD 8.7K) all have negative expected net margins, so I wouldn't run them.

### Next steps
I haven't created a draft yet. If you want it, I'll set up the brief and draft audience from this spec. You'd then open it in the Audience builder, review and lock the audience, and have content approved.
